name: nih-r01-competing-renewal
description: When NIH announces a brand-new R01 award, will that project later be continued through a competing-renewal award on the same core project number, or will the project end without one?
split_description: One row per new award; assignment by AWARD_NOTICE_DATE with hard fiscal-year boundaries (Oct 1 - Sep 30) and no shuffling: train FY2008-FY2012, eval FY2013-FY2014, holdout FY2015-FY2016; FY2017 is held back as a post-holdout drift check and never used for tuning. No calendar embargo gap is imposed, because every feature for a row is restricted to records dated strictly before that row's notice date, and every label uses only post-decision records of that same core project; instead right-censoring is enforced by requiring the full 6-year window to be observed at the data cutoff. Identity/aggregate features additionally obey the rule that they may use only cohorts whose outcome window closed before the decision instant, so a later row can never disclose an earlier row's target.
